task.title: Input parser drops application-mode arrow keys (SS3), breaking Lemonhunt turning
task.body:
## Summary

Limoni v0.9.2's `core/driver/parser.go` recognizes normal-mode arrow keys (`CSI A/B/C/D`), but its SS3 branch recognizes only F1–F4 (`SS3 P/Q/R/S`). Application-mode arrows (`SS3 A/B/C/D`) are consumed without producing a key event.

This makes Lemonhunt's left/right turning controls unresponsive when the terminal is in application cursor-key mode (DECCKM).

## Observed scenario

Running the published Lemonhunt module (`v0.0.0-20260926154851-031f5bd58bd7`, which depends on Limoni v0.9.2) in Hex1b's web-terminal demo:

```sh
go install github.com/thebanri/limoni/apps/lemonhunt@latest
lemonhunt
```

The configured zsh emits `ESC [ ? 1 h` to enable application cursor keys and does not disable that mode before launching commands. Hex1b consequently sends the standard application-mode arrow sequences. Limoni's fullscreen setup does not reset DECCKM, and the parser discards those inputs.

Lemonhunt works in Ghostty in the reported environment. Its negotiated Kitty keyboard protocol provides a different input path, so that result alone does not exercise legacy SS3 arrow handling.

## Minimal parser reproduction

Run against `github.com/thebanri/limoni v0.9.2`:

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/thebanri/limoni/core/driver"
)

func main() {
    for _, wire := range []string{
        "\x1b[D", "\x1b[C", // normal left/right
        "\x1bOD", "\x1bOC", // application left/right
    } {
        ev, consumed := driver.ParseEvent([]byte(wire))
        fmt.Printf("bytes=%X consumed=%d keyEvent=%v\n",
            wire, consumed, ev.Type == driver.EventKey)
    }
}
```

Observed output:

```text
bytes=1B5B44 consumed=3 keyEvent=true
bytes=1B5B43 consumed=3 keyEvent=true
bytes=1B4F44 consumed=3 keyEvent=false
bytes=1B4F43 consumed=3 keyEvent=false
```

## Expected behavior

Recognize application-mode arrows as the same logical keys as their normal-mode counterparts:

| Key | Normal mode | Application mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up | `ESC [ A` | `ESC O A` |
| Down | `ESC [ B` | `ESC O B` |
| Right | `ESC [ C` | `ESC O C` |
| Left | `ESC [ D` | `ESC O D` |

## Suggested fix

Extend the `case 'O'` SS3 branch in [`core/driver/parser.go`](https://github.com/thebanri/limoni/blob/v0.9.2/core/driver/parser.go) to recognize `A/B/C/D`, preserving existing F1–F4 handling. Application-mode Home/End (`SS3 H/F`) appear to have the same omission and are worth covering too. Add regression tests for complete and fragmented sequences.

## Workaround

Reset DECCKM immediately before launching Lemonhunt, on the same command line so the shell cannot re-enable it between commands:

```sh
printf '\033[?1l'; lemonhunt
```

The parser mismatch was reproduced directly against v0.9.2, and the shell mode transitions were captured locally. The workaround's reset-before-child ordering was verified; the game itself was not re-tested end-to-end with the workaround.
